name: DDL scheduler must preserve local processing fact across owner handoff

payload.p_check: RetireOwnerHook fires because the TiDB instance lost DDL ownership during a topology fault; code assumes owner retirement means local DDL scheduling state can be discarded.
payload.q_claim: owner retirement does not mean already-delivered local worker goroutines have stopped; if the same instance becomes owner again before those goroutines return, the dispatcher must still remember processing job IDs and must not dispatch the same DDL job a second time

boundary.before: a long ADD INDEX ingest/reorg job has been delivered to a worker and runningJobs.processingIDs contains the job ID
boundary.fault: owner/PD topology handoff invokes RetireOwnerHook and the instance may later become owner again
boundary.after: getJob/loadDDLJobAndRun observes runningJobs and decides whether to dispatch a job

name: DDL processing job ID survives owner retire

payload.contract: If a DDL job has already been delivered to a local worker, owner retirement must not make that same job locally runnable again before the worker returns.
minimal_observation: create a runningJobs instance and add one job
verify checkRunnable(job) is false while it is processing
apply the revision's retire semantics: fixed revisions use clear(), vulnerable revisions replace runningJobs
RED if checkRunnable(job) becomes true after retire
GREEN if checkRunnable(job) remains false after retire

red_signature.failure: Should be false after retire semantics

Does not assert final ADD INDEX job state; it proves the root duplicate-dispatch guard
reusable_for: other local worker registries that exclude active IDs from durable queues
topology faults where old goroutines can overlap with new ownership

rationale: the verified oracle is the narrow processingIDs preservation boundary proven by issue51846
